properties.description:

* WHERE...Far northeast Grant County in central Indiana...
Far northeast Jay County in east central Indiana...
Southern Adams County in northeastern Indiana...
Southeast Huntington County in northeastern Indiana...
Wells County in northeastern Indiana...

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring.

has come to an end early this afternoon. Isolated to scattered

warned area.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued September 16 at 3:17PM MST until September 16 at 6:15PM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
FFWFGZ

The National Weather Service in Flagstaff has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
The North Canyon, South Canyon, and Nankoweap washes downstream of
the Dragon Bravo Fire scar in...
Coconino County in north central Arizona...

* Until 615 PM MST /715 PM MDT/.

* At 317 PM MST /417 PM MDT/, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms
producing heavy rain over the North Canyon, South Canyon, and
Nankoweap washes downstream of the Dragon Bravo Fire scar. Between
1.5 and 2.5 inches of rain have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts
up to 1 inch are possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is
ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding in and around the North Canyon and South
Canyon washes downstream of the Dragon Bravo Fire scar.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around the
North Canyon, South Canyon, and Nankoweap washes
downstream of the Dragon Bravo Fire scar.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Saddle Mountain Overlook, Point Imperial Picnic Area, Roosevelt
Point Overlook, Saddle Mountain Wilderness, Bert Loper's Boat,
Royal Arches, Triple Alcoves, Point Hansbrough, Anasazi Foot
Bridge, North Rim Entrance Station, Vista Encantada, Kwagunt Valley
and Malgosa Canyon.

State Route 67 between mile markers 609 and 610. the Colorado River
between river miles 17 and 21...and near river mile 32...and between
river miles 37 and 47...and between river miles 52 and 57.

House Rock Camp Site, Upper South Canyon Camp Site, South Canyon Camp
Site, Tatahatso Wash Camp Site, Tatahatso Camp Site, Above Martha's
Camp Site, Martha's Camp Site, Redbud Alcove Camp Site, MCD Site Camp
Site, Upper Buck Farm Camp Site, Buck Farm Camp Site, Below Buck Farm
Camp Site, Loper's Boat Camp Site, Royal Arches Camp Site, Anasazi

ground immediately! Stay away or be swept away!

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued September 16 at 4:44PM MDT until September 16 at 6:30PM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
At 444 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing heavy
rain over the Seven Cabins Burn Scar. Between 0.75 and 1.75 inches of
rain have fallen. The expected rainfall rate is 1 to 2 inches in 1
hour. Additional rainfall amounts up to 1 inch are possible in the
warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

Excessive rainfall over the burn scar will impact Highway 246 as well
as Forest Service Roads 56 and 616. This will also impact Las Tablas
Creek and Arroyo Seco. The debris flow can consist of rock, mud,
vegetation and other loose materials.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding in and around the Seven Cabins Burn Scar.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around the
Seven Cabins Burn Scar.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Mainly rural areas of East Central Lincoln County.
properties.instruction:
This is a life threatening situation. Heavy rainfall will cause
extensive and severe flash flooding of creeks, streams and ditches in
the Seven Cabins Burn Scar. Severe debris flows can also be
anticipated across roads. Roads and driveways may be washed away in
places. If you encounter flood waters, climb to safety.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued September 16 at 3:10PM EDT by NWS Tampa Bay Ruskin FL
properties.description:
...The National Weather Service in Tampa Bay Ruskin has issued a
Flood Warning for the following rivers in Florida...

Withlacoochee At US 41 Dunnellon affecting Citrus, Marion and Levy
Counties.

.The Withlacoochee River at Dunnellon (US 41) has been steadily
rising since July and on September 15, reached flood stage. The cause
of the high water along the Withlacoochee River at Dunnellon is
excessive hydrilla growth (from river bottom to the water surface)
along a 4.5 mile stretch of river between US 41 and Lake Rousseau.
The hydrilla is acting like a dam and holding water back, causing
water levels to rise.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Withlacoochee at US 41 Dunnellon.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 28.2 feet, Docks and boat ramps flood along the river
in Citrus and Marion counties.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 2:45 PM EDT Wednesday the stage was 28.3 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 28.2 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 2:45 PM EDT Wednesday was 28.3 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to remain steady above flood
stage at 28.3 feet.
- Flood stage is 28.2 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 28.3
feet on 10/05/1965.
- https://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 1145 PM EDT.

issued a Flood Warning for the following rivers in Kansas...

Counties.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Stranger Creek at Easton.

* WHEN...From this afternoon to Friday morning.

Easton. At 18.0 feet, 1st street in Easton and 231st street north

inches across the eastbound lane. At 21.5 feet, Most of Easton east
